summary: This note is the reference page for the Snowflake system function SYSTEM$TYPEOF, which returns a VARCHAR string naming the SQL data type of an input expression. It gives the syntax SYSTEM$TYPEOF( <expr> ), where the argument can be a column name or a general expression, and lists example outputs for NULL, integer, scientific-notation, and string literals and a CONCAT expression. The Usage Notes section is empty.
one_line: Reference page for the SYSTEM$TYPEOF function, which returns the SQL data type name of an expression with examples.
key_facts: SYSTEM$TYPEOF returns a string representing the SQL data type associated with an expression.
The argument can be a column name or a general expression.
The function returns a VARCHAR that contains the data type of the input expression.
The note gives BOOLEAN, DECIMAL, ARRAY and OBJECT as examples of returned data type names.
The examples are run with FROM (values(1)) v as the source table.
The page sits under the Query Information category of the documentation.
The Usage Notes section of the page has no content.
